newsitem.title: LEBANON: Blast wounds three Israeli-backed militiamen.
newsitem.headline: Blast wounds three Israeli-backed militiamen.

text.p: A roadside bomb exploded near a patrol of Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) militiamen in south Lebanon on Thursday, wounding three militiamen, SLA sources said.
They said the blast occurred as the SLA patrol passed in the Shoumariyyeh area on the edge of the central sector of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.

In a second incident, guerrillas clashed with Israeli forces in the Arqoub area in the eastern sector of the border zone, the SLA sources added. There was no immediate word on casualties in the exchange of fire.
No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attacks but pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) and other guerrillas wage attacks almost daily against Israeli and SLA forces in south Lebanon.

Some 1,000 Israeli troops and the 3,000-strong SLA control the 15-km (nine-mile)-wide zone in south Lebanon set up by the Jewish state in 1985 to protect its northern settlements from cross-frontier raids.
